title: Tea tree and witch hazel toner
subtitle: A clarifying toner for oily and blemish-prone skin
excerpt: A water-based toner of alcohol-free witch hazel, tea tree essential oil, and aloe vera juice for oily and blemish-prone skin. Apply with a cotton pad after cleansing. Makes 100 ml; keeps three months.
sourceNotes: Witch hazel (Hamamelis virginiana) as an astringent toner: CIR safety assessment and general dermatology reference. Tea tree oil antimicrobial properties in skincare: Carson, C. F. et al., Clinical Microbiology Reviews (2006). Aloe vera juice in cosmetics: general cosmetic science reference on humectant and skin-conditioning properties.

recipe.yieldDescription: 100 ml toner (~100 applications with a cotton pad)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make 100 ml at a time; the aloe vera juice limits the shelf life.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps three months in a sealed amber bottle in the fridge. The aloe vera juice is the life-limiting ingredient; without a preservative, the toner degrades beyond three months. Discard if the liquid turns cloudy, smells sour, or changes colour.

glossaryTerms.definition: A steam-distilled extract from the bark and leaves of Hamamelis virginiana. Used as a mild astringent toner to reduce the appearance of pores and remove traces of oil and impurities after cleansing. Alcohol-free witch hazel is less drying than the traditional alcohol-based extract.

content.text: This is a light water-based toner for oily and combination skin.

forms the base; aloe vera juice adds a small amount of humectancy; tea tree essential oil provides some antimicrobial action against surface bacteria. The alcohol-free witch hazel is gentler than the traditional formulation and suitable for most skin types. Apply with a cotton pad after cleansing and before moisturising.
Tea tree essential oil is toxic to cats. Patch test on the jaw for 24 hours before first full use.

items.prepNote: alcohol-free witch hazel extract; the main base
cosmetic-grade aloe vera juice (not gel); adds light humectancy
approximately 0.25 ml; keeps the dosage skin-safe at well under 1%

content.text: Combine the witch hazel and aloe vera juice in the bottle.
Add the tea tree essential oil drops.
Fit the cap and shake gently to blend. Label with the date.

Shake before each use. Saturate a cotton pad and sweep gently across the face after cleansing. Avoid the eye area. Follow with a moisturiser. Use morning and night or morning only if the skin feels dry after evening use.
Keeps three months in a sealed bottle in the fridge. The aloe vera juice limits the shelf life; this toner does not contain a preservative. Discard if the liquid turns cloudy or smells sour.
